description:
## Outcome

The CLI can enable the trusted coding pack by default, disable it, or replace it by ID. Interactive sessions load bounded project instructions and resolve `@file` mentions through the workspace service.

## Why now

The pack is now safe and useful. This story makes it the default coding use case without hard-wiring any tool into Jidoka or the TUI.

## Current state

`Jido.Cli.DefaultAgent` has a short prompt and no tools. TUI editor accepts plain text only. The CLI has no coding profile selection, instruction presentation, or file mention resolver. The extension bridge and workspace/read tools now supply public seams.

## Ownership and boundary

This is a `jido_cli` change. Trusted host defaults choose extension/profile IDs and workspace root. Jidoka owns pack tools, path/ignore rules, policy, and session context. The CLI owns configuration precedence, TUI editor behavior, visible provenance, and prompt context selection.

## Detailed implementation

1. Add CLI configuration for default coding pack ID and execution profile ID, with explicit enable, disable, and replacement states.
2. Resolve defaults through the same trusted extension and profile paths as explicit agent requests. Never name a module in data.
3. At session start, request bounded project instructions from the coding workspace service. Show the loaded files and order in the TUI and attach their data/provenance as Jidoka context.
4. Extend editor parsing for escaped literal `@` and file mentions. Resolve matches only through `coding.search/read`, ignore rules, and size limits.
5. Show clear errors for ignored, ambiguous, missing, binary, oversized, or denied mentions without submitting unsafe context.
6. Keep default tools independently removable and replaceable.
7. Add noninteractive behavior: no fuzzy prompt; ambiguous mention is a configuration/input error if mentions are supported there.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] First-run trusted configuration enables the pack and profile without a module name.
- [ ] Users can disable the full pack or replace an individual tool through trusted IDs.
- [ ] Project instructions load in deterministic documented order with visible provenance.
- [ ] `@file` cannot select ignored or outside-root data.
- [ ] Literal `@`, missing, ambiguous, binary, and oversized cases behave clearly.
- [ ] Interactive and automated sessions use the same Jidoka context and tool contracts.

## Test plan

- Success: default, disabled, replacement, nested instructions, exact mention, and escaped literal mention.
- Invalid input: unknown pack/profile, ambiguous file, bad config, and malformed mention.
- Runtime failure: workspace resolver, read tool, extension startup, and instruction load failures.
- Boundary and security: ignored secret, symlink escape, untrusted project, raw module/command config, and size limit.
- Deterministic capability: inject config, registry, trust, workspace/search/read services, terminal, clock, and IDs.
- JSONL and exit status: automation stdout stays JSONL; configuration/trust failures exit 64 and runtime failures exit 1.

## Documentation

Update README first-run coding instructions, configuration precedence, default tools, disable/replace examples, project instruction order, `@file`, and constrained-execution setup.

## Non-goals

Do not add TUI diff review yet. Do not add fuzzy UI beyond file mention selection needs. Do not add LSP, browser, MCP, plans, tasks, or subagents.

## Dependencies

Blocking issues:

- `jido_cli-tqg.4.7` — Resolve trusted extensions and project trust in both CLI modes
- `jido_cli-tqg.5.2` — Add removable read and search coding tools
- `jido_cli-tqg.5.4` — Add a bounded constrained shell tool
- `jido_cli-tqg.5.5` — Add Git review tools and named verification helpers

Features unlocked by this story:

- Interactive edit review
- A useful first-run coding experience

## Commit plan

Create exactly one focused `jido_cli` commit. Use a message such as `feat(cli): enable the selectable coding setup (jido_cli-tqg.5.6)`. Do not include another backlog feature.

## Verification commands

```sh
cd /Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_cli/jido_cli
mix test test/jido_cli/coding_setup_test.exs test/jido_cli/cli/tui/editor_test.exs test/jido_cli/cli/tui_test.exs
mix quality
mix test --cover
mix docs
```
title: Make the default coding setup selectable and context-aware
